title: A Sequence-to-Sequence Approach with Mixed Pointers to Topic Segmentation and Segment Labeling

problem.claim: The task is to divide text into semantically coherent segments and assign topic labels to those segments.

gap.claim: Existing generative models struggle to accurately generate strings of segment boundaries, limiting their competitiveness.

contributions.claim: Seq2Seq-MP uses an encoder-decoder architecture with pointer mechanisms to generate segment boundaries and topics.
The approach introduces pairwise type encoding and type-aware relative position encoding to improve fusion of type and position information and interactions between sentences and topics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Seq2Seq-MP as a novel sequence-to-sequence approach with mixed pointers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public datasets reportedly show that Seq2Seq-MP outperforms the current state-of-the-art, with improvements of up to 2.9% in Pk and 4.0% in F1.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines topic segmentation and segment labeling.
Summarizes prior model families and identifies boundary-generation limitations in existing generative models.
Introduces Seq2Seq-MP with mixed pointers for generating boundaries and topics.
Adds pairwise type encoding and type-aware relative position encoding.
Reports state-of-the-art performance on public datasets with gains in Pk and F1.

source_observation.claim: Pointer mechanisms are used to generate segment boundaries and topics, while encoding additions improve type-position fusion.

interpretation.claim: Structured output generation may address boundary-generation difficulties while preserving interactions between sentence and topic information.

application.claim: For tasks requiring structured boundaries and labels, consider pointer-based generation combined with explicit type and relative-position representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices generalize beyond topic segmentation and segment labeling.
